newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Cisco, 3Com busy as stocks drop.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Cisco, 3Com busy as stocks drop.

text.p: Options on some networking stocks, led by Cisco Systems Inc and 3Com Corp, were active Tuesday as the shares fell.
3Com shares were down 3-3/4 at 58-1/4 Tuesday afternoon on heavy volume of more than 23.1 million shares.
Cisco Systems lost 1-7/8 to 66-3/8 on volume of about 15.8 million shares.
Cisco's fiscal second quarter earnings are scheduled to be released after the market close.
Patrick Hamilton at LETCO in Chicago, said early demand for put options on Cisco had eased by afternoon.
"Initially I thought maybe the earnings weren't going to be as good, but now I don't see the rush" for those puts, he said, adding that volatilities also began to come in.
Volatilities that normally trade in the 40 region reached the 60 area Monday almost across the board, he said.
Analysts' consensus expectations for Cisco's quarterly earnings are $0.50 a share, but some expectations are around $0.52, traders said.
On the CBOE, the Cisco February 65 put was the most active put, with volume of nearly 3,550 contracts. The February 60 put traded 1,860 and the February 70 traded 1,515.
The March 60 and 65 puts and the April 65 and 70 put were fairly busy.
On the call side, the Cisco February 70 call traded about 5,525 contracts, the February 65 traded nearly 4,600 and the February 75 traded about 2,375.
Analysts said network stocks were hit by renewed fears of a December sales slowdown at 3Com and that investors were jittery that slowing growth may be an industry-wide issue.
Last week, 3Com executives told analysts that a sales slowdown had hit the company in December but that sales had recovered in January.
The most active 3Com options were the February 55 and 60 calls, which traded 5,500 and 5,150 contracts, respectively. The busiest put was the February 55 with volume of about 4,430 contracts.
Steady activity was seen in most puts and calls in 3Com from the February series through the July series.
Two 3Com LEAPS (long term equity anticipation securities), the January 1998 90 call and the January 1999 45 put, saw heavy trading.
The January 1998 90 call traded about 2,220 contracts. The January 1999 45 put traded 3,500 contracts.
Five hundred contracts in the January 1998 90 call were part of a straddle and 1,000 of the January 1999 45 put were part of a spread.
A couple of LEAP puts on Intel Corp were active, led by the January 1998 130, which traded 5,005 contracts in a spread. The option had open interest of 3,233.
The January 1998 140 put traded roughly 3,045 contracts. Its open interest was 944. Most of that volume was also a spread.
